title: The Context, Meaning and Scope of Tourism
titleCn: The Context, Meaning and Scope of Tourism
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: The Context, Meaning and Scope of Tourism

A Travel has existed since the beginning of time, when primitive man set out, often traversing great distances in search of game, which provided the food and clothing necessary for his survival. Throughout the course of history, people have travelled for purposes of trade, religious conviction, economic gain, war, migration and other equally compelling motivations. In the Roman era, wealthy aristocrats and high government officials also travelled for pleasure. Seaside resorts located at Pompeii and Herculaneum afforded citizens the opportunity to escape to their vacation villas in order to avoid the summer heat of Rome. Travel, except during the Dark Ages, has continued to grow and, throughout recorded history, has played a vital role in the development of civilisations and their economies.

B Tourism in the mass form as we know it today is a distinctly twentieth-century phenomenon. Historians suggest that the advent of mass tourism began in England during the industrial revolution with the rise of the middle class and the availability of relatively inexpensive transportation. The creation of the commercial airline industry following the Second World War and the subsequent development of the jet aircraft in the 1950s signaled the rapid growth and expansion of international travel. This growth led to the development of major new industry: tourism. In turn, international tourism became the concern of a number of world governments since it not only provided new employment opportunities but also produced a means of earning foreign exchange.

C Tourism today has grown significantly in both economic and social importance. In most industrialised countries over the past few years the fastest growth has been seen in the area of services. One of the largest segments of the service industry, although largely unrecognized as an entity in some of these countries, is travel and tourism. According to the World Travel and Tourism Council (1992), 'Travel and tourism is the largest industry in the world on virtually any economic measure including value-added capital investment, employment and tax contributions'. In 1992, the industry's gross output was estimated to be $3.5 trillion, over 12 per cent of all consumer spending. The travel and tourism industry is the world's largest employer with almost 130 million jobs, or almost 7 per cent of all employees. This industry is the world's leading industrial contributor, producing over 6 per cent of the world's gross national product and accounting for capital investment in excess of $422 billion in direct, indirect and personal taxes each year. Thus, tourism has a profound impact both on the world economy and, because of the educative effect of travel and the effects on employment, on society itself.

D However, the major problems of the travel and tourism industry that have hidden, or obscured, its economic impact are the diversity and fragmentation of the industry itself. The travel industry includes: hotels, motels and other types of accommodation; restaurants and other food services; transportation services and facilities; amusements, attractions and other leisure facilities; gift shops and a large number of other enterprises. Since many of these businesses also serve local residents, the impact of spending by visitors can easily be overlooked or underestimated. In addition, Meis (1992) points out that the tourism industry involves concepts that have remained amorphous to both analysts and decision makers. Moreover, in all nations this problem has made it difficult for the industry to develop any type of reliable or credible tourism information base in order to estimate the contribution it makes to regional, national and global economies. However, the nature of this very diversity makes travel and tourism ideal vehicles for economic development in a wide variety of countries, regions or communities.

E Once the exclusive province of the wealthy, travel and tourism have become an institutionalized way of life for most of the population. In fact, McIntosh and Goeldner (1990) suggest that tourism has become the largest commodity in international trade for many nations and, for a significant number of other countries, it ranks second or third. For example, tourism is the major source of income in Bermuda, Greece, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and most Caribbean countries. In addition, Hawkins and Ritchie, quoting from data published by the American Express Company, suggest that the travel and tourism industry is the number one ranked employer in the Bahamas, Brazil, Canada, France, (the former) West Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States. However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact. In many cases, similar difficulties arise when attempts are made to measure domestic tourism.

groups.instruction:
Questions 1-4

Reading Passage 1 has five paragraphs, A-E.

Choose the correct heading for paragraphs S -E from the list of headings below.

Write the correct number, i-v ii，in boxes 1-4 on your answer sheet.

Example Answer

Paragraph A viii

questions.explanation:
题号：1

参考译文：大众旅游业的发展

定位词：development, mass

B段：实际上，本段第一句话就开宗明义，点明此段主要谈及tourism in the mass form，我们今天所熟知的大众旅游是20世纪的产物，接下来各句逐步展开，分别提到它的源起、促成因素、发展过程和影响等。

需要特别注意的是，本段中两次提及“飞行”在大众旅游业的发展中所起作用，因此vi项“航空旅行对旅游业的贡献”容易被误选为正确答案。但浏览完全段内容后就不难看出: “航空旅行”只是大众旅游业发展进程中的许多因素之一，并不能代表本段的主旨内容，因此vi项是在以偏概全。正确选项为ii。

题号：2

参考译文：旅游观光业在经济和社会方面的重要性

定位词：economic, social, significance

C段：本段是一个极其规则的“总分总”结构的段落。段首第一句话提纲挈领地指出“今日的旅游业在经济和社会方面都已成为举足轻重的因素”，段尾最后一句话又重申“旅游业对经济和社会本身都具有深远影响力”。中间部分则是举出种种数据的实例来支持这一论点，对于考生来说，选出正确答案i项应当不是难事。

题号：3

参考译文：认证旅游业所具经济影响力的困难性

定位词：difficulty, recognising, economic effects

D段：本段的解题难度依然不高，因为基本遵循了“总分”+“过渡句开启下段内容"的常见划段模式。段首第一句即点明了：旅游业自身的多样性和分化性造成了很难评估其影响力的问题。接下来的行文分别给出了具体解说并引用人言来支持此论点。结尾句话锋一转指出：虽然这些属性造成了问题，但同时也是机遇。这句话为下文继续论述旅游业的优势开启了话端。纵观全段内容，主体在于强调此行业的问题，因此正确答案为v。

题号：4

参考译文：旅游观光业在全球的影响力

定位词：world impact

E段：此篇的选择段落大意题从总体上说都不困难，E段仍然沿用了“总分”的段落结构，段首的两句即点明主旨：旅游观光已经成为大多数人的生活方式之一，此行业在大多数国家中的重要性排名都可跻身前三。接下来段落列举了大量国家名称作为佐证，强调旅游业在全球范围内的巨大影响。正确答案为vi。

groups.instruction:
Questions 5-10

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information,

choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information,

or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt:
The largest employment figures in the world are found in the travel and tourism

industry.
questions.explanation:
译文：全球最大的就业数字出现在旅游观光业（即旅游观光业的从业人数是全球所有行业中排名第一的）。

定位词：Largest employment figures, world

C段：The travel and tourism industry is the world's largest employer with almost 130 million jobs, or almost 7 per cent of all employees.

其实这道题只需看懂题干就不难定位，题目只是把原文中的largest employer替换为largest employment figures，答案为TRUE。employer 在本篇文章中并非广大考生所熟悉的“雇主”之意，而是借用了构词法employ+er的方式，以表示“发出雇用动作者”，结合文意，准确的理解为“雇佣行业”。

questions.prompt: Tourism contributes over six per cent of the Australian gross national product.
questions.explanation:
译文：旅游业对澳大利亚国民生产总值的贡献超过了6%。

定位词：six per cent, Australian gross national product

C段：This industry is the world's leading industrial contributor, producing over 6 per cent of the world's gross national product and...

“6%”不难定位，就在文中C段紧跟第5题后面的位置，且还是比较醒目的阿拉伯数字“6”，但认真看过全句后会发现，这个旅游业对国民生产总值6%的贡献是就全球范围而言，原文中并未明确说到在全球的每一个国家都超过了6%。更加谨慎的考生可能会继续向下追踪两句，但再无信息提及“澳大利亚”或“国民生产总值”，因此答案为NOT GIVEN。这是一道典型的“缩小原文所指范围”的题目，相当于原文说“他是中国人”而题干说“他是北京人”，两者既不相同也不矛盾，属于“there is no information on this"的范畴。

questions.prompt: Tourism has a social impact because it promotes recreation.
questions.explanation:
译文：旅游业由于宣传推广娱乐休闲而有着社会影响力。

定位词：social impact, promotes recreation

C段：Thus, tourism has a profound impact both on the world economy and, because of the educative effect of travel and the effects on employment, on society itself.

此句确实提到了旅游业具有影响社会的力量，也给出了原因是“教育”和“就业”，但“宣传推广娱乐休闲”与此二者并非同类的相似关系，也非相反的矛盾关系，所以答案是NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt:
Two main features of the travel and tourism industry make its economic significance

difficult to ascertain.
questions.explanation:
译文：旅游观光业有两个主要特点使得其在经济上的重要性很难得到确认。

定位词：Two main features, economic significance, difficult to ascertain

D段：However, the major problems of the travel and tourism industry that have hidden, or obscured, its economic impact are the diversity and fragmentation of the industry itself.

要正确解答此题，主要需看懂句子主干major problems are diversity and fragmentation，如果不认识“多样性”和“分化性”这两个词，并不影响解题。这是一道常见的同义替换类型的TRUE。

questions.prompt: Visitor spending is always greater than the spending of residents in tourist areas.
questions.explanation:
译文：在旅游区，游客总是比本地居民消费得更多。

定位词：Visitor spending, always greater, residents

D段：Since many of these businesses also serve local residents, the impact of spending by visitors can easily be overlooked or underestimated.

题干中的Visitor spending回到原文只是稍微改换了顺序变成spending by visitors，定位并不困难。但是原文也并没有将游客消费与本地居民消费进行比较，所以答案为NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: It is easy to show statistically how tourism affects individual economies.
questions.explanation:
译文：很容易用数据来显示旅游业是如何影响到各国经济的。

定位词：easy, statistically, affects, individual economies

E段：However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact.

本题的难点一来自于对题干中individual economies的理解，二来自对应原文的长难句理解。economy 本身是个抽象名词，指“经济”这一领域，world economy当然指“全球经济”这个总体范围，而individual economy却不能简单地累加其中文意思变成“个体经济”，而是指各个国家自己的经济，组合起来也就是原文中world-wide tourism在全球范围内对每一个国家的economic impact。本句的详细解析可以参见前文，大意为很难就其经济影响提供可靠数据，与题干相矛盾，因此答案为FALSE。

groups.instruction:
Questions 11-13

Complete the sentences below.

Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the text in each gap.

questions.prompt: In Greece, tourism is the most important [11] ______ .
questions.explanation:
题号：11

定位词：Greece

For example, tourism is the major source of income in Bermuda, Greece, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and most Caribbean countries.通过定位词很容易找到文中定位句，此句中的major对应most important，所以答案为source of income。

题号：12

定位词：Jamaica

In addition, Hawkins and Ritchie, quoting from data published by the American Express Company, suggest that the travel and tourism industry is the number one ranked employer in the Bahamas, Brazil, ..., Jamaica, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States.同样依据Jamaica这个定位词很好找到原句，number one ranked对应题干中的major，答案为employer。再次温馨提示：在本文中 “employer”不可理解为“雇主”，而是指需要发生雇佣关系的行业。

题号：13

定位词：Problems, measuring international tourism, reflected, measurement

However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact. In many cases, similar difficulties arise when attempts are made to measure domestic tourism.此题的定位由于缩小了范围而并不困难，但要成功锁定正确答案则要稍费一番周折。原文中表述“很难衡量国际旅游业影响”的那一句并没有提及这些问题还在哪里被反映了出来，需要考生在确认此句没有正确答案后当机立断，果断再向下看一句，才能顺利找到measure后面的正确答案domestic tourism。

questions.prompt: The travel and tourism industry in Jamaica is the major [12] ______
questions.explanation:
题号：11

定位词：Greece

For example, tourism is the major source of income in Bermuda, Greece, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and most Caribbean countries.通过定位词很容易找到文中定位句，此句中的major对应most important，所以答案为source of income。

题号：12

定位词：Jamaica

In addition, Hawkins and Ritchie, quoting from data published by the American Express Company, suggest that the travel and tourism industry is the number one ranked employer in the Bahamas, Brazil, ..., Jamaica, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States.同样依据Jamaica这个定位词很好找到原句，number one ranked对应题干中的major，答案为employer。再次温馨提示：在本文中 “employer”不可理解为“雇主”，而是指需要发生雇佣关系的行业。

题号：13

定位词：Problems, measuring international tourism, reflected, measurement

However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact. In many cases, similar difficulties arise when attempts are made to measure domestic tourism.此题的定位由于缩小了范围而并不困难，但要成功锁定正确答案则要稍费一番周折。原文中表述“很难衡量国际旅游业影响”的那一句并没有提及这些问题还在哪里被反映了出来，需要考生在确认此句没有正确答案后当机立断，果断再向下看一句，才能顺利找到measure后面的正确答案domestic tourism。

In Greece, tourism is the most important  [11] ______ .

The travel and tourism industry in Jamaica is the major  [12] ______

The problems associated with measuring international tourism are often reflected in the measurement of  [13] ______.

articleHtml:
The Context, Meaning and Scope of Tourism

A    Travel has existed since the beginning of time, when primitive man set out, often traversing great distances in search of game, which provided the food and clothing necessary for his survival. Throughout the course of history, people have travelled for purposes of trade, religious conviction, economic gain, war, migration and other equally compelling motivations. In the Roman era, wealthy aristocrats and high government officials also travelled for pleasure. Seaside resorts located at Pompeii and Herculaneum afforded citizens the opportunity to escape to their vacation villas in order to avoid the summer heat of Rome. Travel, except during the Dark Ages, has continued to grow and, throughout recorded history, has played a vital role in the development of civilisations and their economies.

1[1] ______

B    Tourism in the mass form as we know it today is a distinctly twentieth-century phenomenon. Historians suggest that the advent of mass tourism began in England during the industrial revolution with the rise of the middle class and the availability of relatively inexpensive transportation. The creation of the commercial airline industry following the Second World War and the subsequent development of the jet aircraft in the 1950s signaled the rapid growth and expansion of international travel. This growth led to the development of major new industry: tourism. In turn, international tourism became the concern of a number of world governments since it not only provided new employment opportunities but also produced a means of earning foreign exchange.

2[2] ______

C    Tourism today has grown significantly in both economic and social importance. In most industrialised countries over the past few years the fastest growth has been seen in the area of services. One of the largest segments of the service industry, although largely unrecognized as an entity in some of these countries, is travel and tourism. According to the World Travel and Tourism Council (1992), 'Travel and tourism is the largest industry in the world on virtually any economic measure including value-added capital investment, employment and tax contributions'. In 1992, the industry's gross output was estimated to be $3.5 trillion, over 12 per cent of all consumer spending. The travel and tourism industry is the world's largest employer with almost 130 million jobs, or almost 7 per cent of all employees. This industry is the world's leading industrial contributor, producing over 6 per cent of the world's gross national product and accounting for capital investment in excess of $422 billion in direct, indirect and personal taxes each year. Thus, tourism has a profound impact both on the world economy and, because of the educative effect of travel and the effects on employment, on society itself.

3[3] ______

D    However, the major problems of the travel and tourism industry that have hidden, or obscured, its economic impact are the diversity and fragmentation of the industry itself. The travel industry includes: hotels, motels and other types of accommodation; restaurants and other food services; transportation services and facilities; amusements, attractions and other leisure facilities; gift shops and a large number of other enterprises. Since many of these businesses also serve local residents, the impact of spending by visitors can easily be overlooked or underestimated. In addition, Meis (1992) points out that the tourism industry involves concepts that have remained amorphous to both analysts and decision makers. Moreover, in all nations this problem has made it difficult for the industry to develop any type of reliable or credible tourism information base in order to estimate the contribution it makes to regional, national and global economies. However, the nature of this very diversity makes travel and tourism ideal vehicles for economic development in a wide variety of countries, regions or communities.

4[4] ______

E     Once the exclusive province of the wealthy, travel and tourism have become an institutionalized way of life for most of the population. In fact, McIntosh and Goeldner (1990) suggest that tourism has become the largest commodity in international trade for many nations and, for a significant number of other countries, it ranks second or third. For example, tourism is the major source of income in Bermuda, Greece, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and most Caribbean countries. In addition, Hawkins and Ritchie, quoting from data published by the American Express Company, suggest that the travel and tourism industry is the number one ranked employer in the Bahamas, Brazil, Canada, France, (the former) West Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States. However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact. In many cases, similar difficulties arise when attempts are made to measure domestic tourism.
